note: Block Inactive Users blocks accounts idle for N months on cron (with warn + reactivation emails) and offers a separate bulk Cancel Users tool. Two config objects: block_inactive_users.settings (key block_inactive_users_idle_time = idle months as a STRING; send_email bool; email_subject; exclude_roles; warn keys; days_until_blocked) and block_inactive_users.settings_cancel_users (idle_time; disable_account_method = a core user_cancel method id; include_roles/status; whitelists; cancel_email). Shipped defaults: settings idle_time '3', send_email false, email_subject 'User disabled.'; settings_cancel_users idle_time '0', disable_account_method 'user_cancel_delete'. Settings forms at /admin/config/people/block_inactive_users (+ /cancel_users) gated by 'administer site configuration'. Medium/hard cases read and write those real config keys (no users are actually blocked).

evals.prompt: In the block_inactive_users module, what triggers inactive accounts to actually get blocked, and which config key sets the inactivity threshold (and in what unit)?
evals.expected_output: hook_cron runs the block sweep (or the 'Disable inactive users' button runs it immediately). The threshold is block_inactive_users_idle_time, measured in whole MONTHS; users whose last access is at least that many months old are blocked.

evals.prompt: block_inactive_users provides two admin screens under People. What are they and how do they differ?
evals.expected_output: The main settings form (/admin/config/people/block_inactive_users, config block_inactive_users.settings) configures the cron auto-block. A separate Cancel Users tool (/admin/config/people/block_inactive_users/cancel_users, config block_inactive_users.settings_cancel_users) bulk-cancels accounts via core user_cancel() by role/status/whitelist rules.

evals.prompt: When block_inactive_users blocks a user and email is enabled, how can that user get their account back?
evals.expected_output: The block email (using the [activation-link] token) contains a signed reactivation URL (route block_inactive_users.reactivate_confirm at /reactivate/{user}/confirm/{timestamp}/{hashed_pass}) the user can follow to request re-activation.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, the block_inactive_users auto-block settings have been customized. Inspect the live configuration and report the inactivity threshold (idle time, in months) currently configured for automatically blocking users.
evals.expected_output: block_inactive_users.settings:block_inactive_users_idle_time is '9' (months), and email notification is enabled. Read with `drush cget block_inactive_users.settings block_inactive_users_idle_time`.

evals.prompt: On this site, the block_inactive_users bulk 'Cancel Users' tool has been configured. Inspect the live configuration and report which account cancellation method it will use.

On this Drupal site, configure block_inactive_users so that accounts inactive for 6 months are automatically blocked, an email notification is sent to blocked users, and the block email subject is 'Account disabled due to inactivity'. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: block_inactive_users.settings has block_inactive_users_idle_time '6', block_inactive_users_send_email true, and block_inactive_users_email_subject 'Account disabled due to inactivity'.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, configure the block_inactive_users bulk 'Cancel Users' tool so it targets accounts inactive for 12 months and cancels them using the 'block' method (user_cancel_block). Apply the change to the live site.
